# HMPFL Week 4 Recap: Lockdown, Lineups, and a Little Light Brutality

Another week behind bars, another round of inmates proving they either belong in general population or deserve to be shipped straight to solitary. Let's run the block.

## The Closest Call: A Razor-Thin Transfer

**The Adrian BeatHisSons** vs. **Ruggs, Drugs and TDs** had the whole cell block pressed against the bars. Just 6.23 points separated these two, with Ruggs, Drugs and TDs sneaking out 244.80–238.57. Jared Goff's 57.2-point outing was basically the shiv that won this one — quiet, efficient, and lethal when nobody expected it.

Not to be outdone, **OJ's Denver Bronco** and **DUIiiiiiiii dont know jim** matched that drama almost point for point, with DUIiiiiiiii escaping 245.45–238.70. OJ got a career night from Tetairoa McMillan (67.4 — the single highest score of the week) and still lost. That's not bad luck, inmates, that's a rigged commissary.

## The Biggest Blowout: Cruel and Unusual Punishment

If you're **The Massage Boys**, you may want to request a cellmate transfer after this one. The **Hernandez Hitmen** dropped a 54.58-point beatdown, winning 238.85–184.27. CeeDee Lamb (59.1) and C.J. Stroud (54.6) combined to basically run the yard unsupervised while the guards looked the other way. This wasn't a loss, it was a strip search.

Honorable mention to **The ConVicks**, who put a 29.15-point hurting on **Smack my Diggs up**, powered by Kyren Williams torching the depth chart for 60.4.

## Standout Performances

Beyond McMillan's league-best outburst, **Kenneth Walker** (62.3) helped **Glove Don't Fit, Blitz** survive a shootout against Steve Ruggs, who got a rare QB/RB double-dip himself — Joe Burrow and Kyle Monangai both going for 57.5 apiece. Unfortunately for Steve, that still wasn't enough; Glove Don't Fit, Blitz held on 260.60–253.05 in a genuine track meet.

## Other Yard Talk

Josh Allen's Prison Cell squeaked past Rice, Rice Baby ✨ by 8.07, proving that sometimes surviving the week is its own kind of parole hearing.

Lights out, inmates. Set your lineups — the warden doesn't accept excuses, only waiver claims.
